app.title: Voice workshop
app.subtitle: Radio Survivor: create the voices you hear on the radio
login.heading: Log in
login.intro: This workshop is open on the network: enter the password written in bridge/.env (ATELIER_PASSWORD).
login.locked: Too many failed attempts: try again in {seconds} s.
welcome.title: Welcome to the voice workshop
welcome.text: Here you make the people who answer on the radio in Radio Survivor: who they are, when they listen, what they know, and the jobs they give.
welcome.step1: Pick a voice on the left to change it, or click "+ New voice".
welcome.step2: Fill in the five steps. Nothing is final until you click Save.
welcome.step3: The game reads your voice again within 30 seconds, no restart needed.
voices.title: Voices
status.delivered.help: A voice that comes with the mod, unchanged
status.modified.help: A voice from the mod that you changed
status.removed.help: A voice from the mod that you took off the air
status.outdated.help: The game will replace this copy with the mod's new version the next time it loads the world.
new.title: New voice
new.help: Give it a name. You can start from an empty voice or from a copy of another voice.
editor.removed_help: This voice is off the air: its sheet is empty. Bring back the mod's version to hear it again.
confirm.remove: Take "{name}" off the air? The game drops it within 30 seconds. You can bring it back later.
confirm.restore: Throw away your changes to "{name}" and get the mod's version back (at the next world load)?
confirm.leave: Your changes are not saved. Leave this voice anyway?
checks.title: {n} thing(s) to look at
checks.judge: These are hints only: you can save anyway, the game decides.
checks.saved_anyway: ({n} hint(s) still open: the game will tell if something is wrong.)
who.question: Who is talking on the radio?
who.name: Name
who.id_help: Lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. It becomes the file name.
who.id_locked: The id of a saved voice does not change. To rename it, make a copy.
who.description_placeholder: The nurse who wants to go back to the clinic
who.description_help: For you only: the game does not read it.
choice.state.silent.help: The voice keeps its frequency but does not answer.
choice.state.gone.help: The voice left the radio; its frequency is free again.
choice.state.dead.help: The voice died in the story; its frequency is free again.
where.question: Where can players hear this voice, and when?
where.band_help: Each new game picks one frequency in this band. Pick a band no other voice uses.
where.overlap: This band crosses the band of: {names}.
where.taken: Bands already taken by the mod's voices ({n})
where.fixed_help: MHz with one decimal, separated by commas (for example 145.0).
choice.radio.high_tier.help: A high-end set, for far away voices.
where.hours_help: Game time. A watch can go past midnight (22:00 to 06:00).
where.location: Is this voice on the map?
choice.location.none.help: Nobody knows where this voice hides.
choice.location.fixed.help: A fixed point of the map (give x, y, z).
where.coords_help: Square coordinates; z is the floor (0 = ground).
where.call_one_in: Spontaneous calls (one chance in N each hour)
where.call_one_in_help: 0 or empty: the voice never calls on its own. 5: about one call every five game hours, during its listening hours.
where.call: What the voice says when calling
where.call_help: Written as players will hear it; %1 is replaced by the voice's frequency. Said when the bridge does not write the call.
where.call_placeholder: Anyone out there? This is Mae on %1. Over.
where.call_text_help: Translation key of the mod (voices shipped with the mod).
personality.question: Who is this voice, and what can it do on the radio?
personality.actions_help: Talking is always on. The others let the voice act in the game.
personality.shares_help: When the voice trusts a player, it can give the frequency of one of these voices.
personality.prompt_help: Who the character is, their past, what they know how to do, what they keep to themselves, their tone and their rules on the radio. The AI reads this text to play the voice.
ai.unavailable: The AI of the bridge is not configured. Copy bridge/.env.example to bridge/.env, fill in OPENAI_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_MODEL, then restart the bridge without --offline.
ai.unavailable_short: AI not configured (see the button's tooltip)
ai.describe: Describe the character in a few sentences
ai.describe_placeholder: A tired nurse who left the clinic and wants to go back...
ai.describe_help: In your own words and your own language: who the character is, what happened, what they want, how they talk. The AI writes the personality in English.
ai.replace_confirm: Replace the current personality with this text?
ai.suggest_help: The AI suggests what the voice says to give this mission (English, one sentence).
ai.try_help: Talk to the voice as a player would, with the sheet as it is now (even unsaved). Nothing changes in the game.
ai.try_empty: Say something to start the conversation.
action.mark_map: Mark a place on the map
action.mark_map.help: Puts one of the voice's places on the caller's map.
action.reveal_area.help: Reveals the area around one of the voice's places on the map.
action.place_scene.help: Places a scene in the world.
action.persona_state.help: The voice's mood and supplies change with the talks.
action.propose_trade.help: Sells goods: fill in the Trade panel of step 5.
action.report_mission.help: Players report a job on the radio.
action.share_frequency.help: Gives the frequency of another voice to a trusted caller.
missions.question: What jobs does this voice give?
missions.none: No mission yet: pick a kind below.
mission.story_placeholder: I need to know what is left of my clinic.
mission.story_help: Why the voice asks, in English (200 characters at most).
mission.target_help: The place of the job (a place used as "job place").
mission.target_optional: Leave empty: the game picks a building near the player.
mission.drops_help: Where the goods are left. Nothing ticked: every dead drop of the voice.
mission.no_drop: This voice has no dead drop yet: add a place used as "dead drop".
mission.after_help: The job is offered once this other mission succeeded.
mission.weight_help: When the voice has several missions to give: the ones it offers most often.
mission.scope_help: For "Only after": the player alone, or the whole team.
mission.sets_state_help: A word (like returned) the personality text can talk about.
mission.scout.help: Visit a building and report what you saw.
mission.clear.help: Kill the zombies around a place.
mission.barricade.help: Board up the outside windows and doors of a building.
mission.deliver.help: Leave the requested goods at a dead drop.
mission.retrieve.help: Find the ID card of a missing person and leave it at a dead drop.
mission.item.help: Find one precious object at a place and leave it at a dead drop.
mission.relay.help: Put a working two-way radio, turned on, upstairs or on the roof of a place.
mission.route.help: Go through several places in order, on foot or by car, then report.
mission.signal.help: Light a Signal Smoke signal at a place.
mission.watch.help: Stay near a place for some game hours, then say what you saw.
param.quantity.help: A number, or a range: the game picks one in it.
param.collect_hours.help: Game hours with nobody around before the goods are picked up.
param.label: Its name
param.label.help: What the voice calls the object.
browser.title: Pick an item of the game
browser.more: First {shown} of {n}: narrow the search or pick a category.
browser.none: No item matches. Try another word or "All categories".
browser.sellable_only: Only the items a trader can sell are listed: those with a price in the trade.
lot.name: Name of lot {n}
trade.no_landing: No place is a trade meeting point yet. Add a place and tick "trade meeting".
note.text_intro: What the player reads on the note. Write %1 where the voice's frequency must appear.
note.needs_frequency: One line must hold %1: that is where the frequency is written.
note.own_item: This note uses its own item of the mod (advanced settings, below).
note.corpse_switch: A dead body carrying a walkie-talkie may have it
section.advanced_help: Used by the voices of the mod. A new voice does not need them.
places.title: Places ({n})
places.help: Places the voice knows: a spot to mark on the map, a job place, a dead drop, or a meeting point for trades.
places.ask: Name of the new place (seen on the map):
places.label: Name on the map
places.label_help: Seen by the players: no secret here.
places.at_help: x, y and floor z (0 = ground). Read them in the game with the debug tools or the map.
surveys.title: Recorded in game
surveys.help: Squares recorded in the game with a right click, "Voice workshop: record this place" (in solo, or by an admin). Newest first.
surveys.none: No place recorded yet. In the game, right click a square, then "Voice workshop: record this place".
surveys.unreadable: The recorded places cannot be read: is the bridge running?
surveys.ask: Name of the place on the map (you can change it later):
surveys.known: Already one of the voice's places
use.mark.help: The voice can mark it on a player's map.
use.target.help: A mission can take place here.
rewards.question: What does a player win after a job?
rewards.help: One reward is drawn at random from this list. For each one, choose whether it comes out rarely, normally or often.
rewards.none: No reward: after a job the voice marks one of its places on the map.
reward.cache.help: A bag of goods from a category, left at the voice's first dead drop.
reward.frequency.help: The frequency of another voice this one can pass on (step 3).
reward.stashmap.help: A map of a hidden stash.
advanced.title: To go further
advanced.trade.help: This voice sells goods to the players. Also tick "Trade" in step 3 and add a place used as "trade meeting point".
advanced.note.help: A note found in the loot that gives the voice's frequency.
advanced.note.enable: The frequency is on a note
advanced.category.help: Lists of goods for the voice's deliveries and supply bags. Categories of the mod: {names}.
key.trade.landing.help: Tick the places where the merchant meets the players.
key.trade.every_days.help: One visit of the merchant every N game days (1 to 28).
key.trade.group.help: A lot gathers goods that share a total. Then pick "In the lot" on their lines.
key.trade.item.help: One item per line: its name and how many the merchant brings. The game already knows its weight.
key.note.text.help: 40 bytes per line at most (an accented letter counts as two).
import.drop: Drop a voice sheet (.txt) to import it
import.exists: A voice with this id already exists ({name}). Pick a new id:
check.band_overlap: The band crosses the band of {name}.
check.bad_hours: Listening hours: each watch needs a start and an end that differ.
check.bad_at: A place needs three whole numbers x, y, z (now: {value}).
check.bad_range: {name}: a number, or two numbers lowest first (2-4).
check.unknown_place: {name}: pick one of the voice's places.
check.not_sellable: {value}: a trader cannot sell this item (it has no price in the trade), so no offer could ever include it. Remove the line or pick an item from the list.
check.needs_drop: This mission needs a dead drop: add a place used as "dead drop".
check.unknown_mission: "Only after" names a mission that does not exist: {value}.
check.bad_weight: {name}: the chances must be 1 or more.
code.offline: The workshop does not answer: is the bridge window still open?
code.http_error: The workshop answered with an error.
code.voice_saved: Saved. The game reads it again within 30 seconds.
code.voice_restored: The mod's version comes back at the next world load.
code.bad_id: The id: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, 32 at most.
code.id_mismatch: The id inside the sheet differs from the voice.
code.voice_exists: A voice "{id}" already exists: pick another id.
code.delivered_voice: A voice of the mod cannot be deleted: take it off the air instead.
code.not_delivered: This is your own voice: delete it instead.
code.bad_encoding: The file is not UTF-8 text.
code.forbidden_origin: Request refused: open the workshop from its own address.
code.login_locked: Too many failed attempts: wait a little.
code.io_error: The file could not be written.
code.ai_unavailable: The AI of the bridge is not configured.
code.ai_failed: The AI did not answer: try again in a moment.
code.prompt_too_large: Too long for the AI: shorten the text.
code.sheet_refused: The sheet is not complete yet: fix the points shown before trying the voice.
verdict.title: The game refused this voice, line {line} of the sheet
verdict.silent: Until it is fixed, the game keeps the last version that worked, or the voice stays silent. Fix it and save: the game reads the sheet again within 30 seconds.
verdict.changed: This sheet changed since the game refused it: the game has not read it again yet. It does within 30 seconds if a game is running, otherwise at the next start; its verdict will show here.
verdict.why.unknown_key: The setting "{name}" does not exist here: check its name or remove it.
verdict.why.duplicate_key: The setting "{name}" is written twice: keep a single line.
verdict.why.missing_key: The setting "{name}" is missing: fill it in.
verdict.why.empty_value: The setting "{name}" is empty: give it a value or remove it.
verdict.why.frequency: A frequency is wrong: a number with one decimal (145.0), on the 0.2 step of the radios, no duplicates and no ranges touching each other.
verdict.why.unknown_section: The block "[{name}]" does not exist in the sheet format.
verdict.why.unknown_ref: "{name}" is not defined anywhere in the sheet (place, mission or category).
verdict.why.mission_type: The mission type "{name}" does not exist.
verdict.why.prompt: The personality is missing or empty: write it in the "Personality" step.
verdict.why.encoding: The file is not saved as plain UTF-8: save it from the workshop.
verdict.why.other: The game does not understand this line of the sheet. The game message below says why.
journal.title: Live journal
journal.help: The lines of the bridge (what players say to the voices, replies, errors) and the sheet lines written by the game, live. Read-only, on this machine only: they hold the players’ dialogues.
journal.no_bridge: The bridge is not running (the AI is not configured): only the game lines show here, and the voices do not answer in game.
journal.no_game_log: Game console not found: start the workshop again with --game-log <file> to see the game lines.
journal.game_log_missing: The game console does not exist yet ({path}): its lines will show once the game runs.
help.head.id.what: The internal name of the voice. It is also the name of its file.
help.head.id.tip: Lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter (32 characters at most). Do not change it later.
help.head.name.what: The name of the character, the way they introduce themselves.
help.head.name.game: Players hear it on the radio.
help.head.format.what: The version of the sheet format.
help.head.format.tip: You do not need to touch it: the workshop fills it in for you.
help.head.language.what: The language of the character, in two lowercase letters (en, fr...). The default is en.
help.head.language.game: The calls the voice makes by itself are written in the server's language.
help.head.language.tip: To make it answer in the language of the player, say so in its personality: "Answer in the same language the caller uses."
help.head.frequency_range.what: A band of frequencies. The game picks one frequency in this band when a new game starts and keeps it for the whole game.
help.head.frequency_range.game: The player has to look for the voice by turning the radio dial: it will not be at the same place in every game.
help.head.frequency_range.tip: Choose either a band or fixed frequencies, not both. The band is the recommended choice. Frequencies go from 1.0 to 999.8 MHz, in steps of 0.2.
help.head.frequencies.what: One or more fixed frequencies, the same in every game.
help.head.frequencies.game: Players can write it down once and for all.
help.head.frequencies.tip: Choose either fixed frequencies or a band, not both. A fixed frequency goes in steps of 0.2: 44.6 works, 44.5 does not.
help.head.radio.what: The kind of radio the player needs to talk to this voice.
help.head.radio.any.what: Any radio that can transmit: a walkie-talkie or a ham radio, as long as the band is within its range.
help.head.radio.high_tier.what: Only a big set: the top walkie-talkie, the military radio or the high-end ham radio.
help.head.radio.high_tier.game: A player with a small walkie-talkie will not be able to talk to it.
help.head.radio.high_tier.tip: Useful for a very distant voice.
help.head.listen.what: The hours when the voice is on the radio: always, or ranges in game time.
help.head.listen.game: Outside those hours the voice stays silent and makes no call.
help.head.listen.tip: Write hours with two digits (08:00, not 8:00). 22:00-06:00 goes past midnight.
help.head.location.what: Where the voice is on the map.
help.head.location.tip: For a new voice, "nowhere" is fine.
help.head.location.none.what: It is nowhere on the map.
help.head.location.fixed.what: It is at a precise point of the map, which you give with x, y, z.
help.head.location.rescue.what: The game chooses the place, for a rescue.
help.head.location.rescue.tip: This choice is kept for the rescue of the Whitakers.
help.head.coords.what: The tile where the voice is: x, y, then the floor z (0 = ground floor).
help.head.coords.tip: Only with "at a precise place". Read the numbers on the game map.
help.head.state.what: The state of the voice in the story.
help.head.state.active.what: The voice listens and answers. This is the normal choice.
help.head.state.silent.what: The voice keeps its frequency but does not answer, as if paused.
help.head.state.gone.what: The voice left the radio. Its frequency is free again.
help.head.state.gone.tip: It can come back later if you change this state.
help.head.state.dead.what: The voice is dead in the story. Its frequency is free again.
help.head.shares.what: The other voices whose frequency this one may give away.
help.head.shares.game: The game itself picks an active voice among them and adds it to the notebook of the player.
help.head.shares.tip: Used by the "Give a frequency" action and the "A frequency" reward.
help.head.budget.what: How many requests the voice accepts per real hour. 0: only the general limit of the mod counts.
help.head.budget.game: Beyond that, the voice stays silent until the next hour.
help.head.budget.tip: It keeps the cost of the AI down.
help.head.call_one_in.what: The voice can call by itself. Every game hour, it has one chance in N to make a general call. 0: never.
help.head.call_one_in.game: The player hears it call without having asked anything, during its listening hours.
help.head.call_one_in.tip: A call uses up one request of its budget.
help.head.call_text.what: The name of the text the voice says when it calls and the bridge does not write the call.
help.head.call_text.tip: Required when spontaneous calls are on. Use a new name: do not reuse the one of another voice. A new voice writes its call (call) instead.
help.head.call.what: What the voice says when it calls by itself and the bridge does not write the call, written in the sheet. %1 is replaced by its frequency.
help.head.call.game: Every player listening on its frequency hears this call on the radio.
help.head.call.example: Anyone out there? This is Mae on %1. Over.
help.head.call.tip: Use this text or call_text, not both. 200 bytes at most, without < > ^; % only in %1.
help.head.actions.what: What the voice can do in the game, besides talking.
help.head.actions.game: During the conversation, the AI decides by itself to use an action when it fits. The game then checks every action; if it is refused, the voice still talks.
help.head.actions.tip: A badly written action makes the whole sheet refused: only tick from the list.
help.head.actions.say.what: The voice answers on the radio.
help.head.actions.persona_state.what: The morale and the supplies of the voice change over the calls.
help.head.actions.persona_state.game: It then talks about it by itself, for instance if it moved.
help.head.actions.persona_state.tip: It is only story: nothing changes in the game.
help.head.actions.mark_map.what: The voice puts a marker on the map of the player.
help.head.actions.mark_map.game: It says "I am marking it on your map" and a symbol appears, at one of its places.
help.head.actions.mark_map.tip: It needs at least one place set as "marker to give" (step 4). Only the player who talks sees it.
help.head.actions.reveal_area.what: The voice reveals a neighbourhood on the map of the player.
help.head.actions.reveal_area.game: It describes a place it knows, and the area appears on the map.
help.head.actions.reveal_area.tip: It needs at least one place set as "marker to give". Only the player who talks sees it.
help.head.actions.signal.tip: For now, the game always refuses this action.
help.head.actions.place_cache.tip: This action is kept for the notebook recovery missions: do not set it in a sheet.
help.head.actions.place_scene.tip: For now, the game always refuses this action.
help.head.actions.start_mission.what: The voice gives missions to the player.
help.head.actions.start_mission.game: The player must have the notebook. After a successful mission, they get reputation and a reward.
help.head.actions.start_mission.tip: Choose the missions in step 4. One mission at a time per player and per voice.
help.head.actions.propose_trade.what: The voice sells goods to players.
help.head.actions.propose_trade.game: It sets a meeting for a no-contact exchange.
help.head.actions.propose_trade.tip: Also fill in the Trade panel of step 5: one without the other is refused.
help.head.actions.report_mission.what: Players can report on a mission over the radio.
help.head.actions.share_frequency.what: The voice gives the frequency of another voice to someone it trusts.
help.head.actions.share_frequency.game: The frequency goes into the notebook of the player.
help.head.actions.share_frequency.tip: The possible voices are set with "shares".
help.ui.surveys.what: The squares you recorded while walking in the game: right click a square, "Voice workshop: record this place". The game notes the square, the container on it, the room and the building.
help.ui.surveys.game: "Add to this voice" makes a place at that square, with a suggested name and uses: a container becomes a dead drop, a building a job place and a map mark. Change anything afterwards in the place's card.
help.ui.surveys.example: A dumpster behind the church, recorded in game, becomes the dead drop "Bin - Church".
help.ui.surveys.tip: In solo the menu is always there; in multiplayer, only for an admin. The records are in Zomboid/Lua/batman_RadioSurvivor/workshop-places.txt on the machine that runs the game or the server (the last 200).
help.place.label.what: The name of the place, as players see it on their map.
help.place.label.tip: No secrets here. 48 bytes at most.
help.place.at.what: The tile of the place: x, y, then the floor z (0 = ground floor).
help.place.at.game: The AI never sees these numbers.
help.place.at.tip: Read them on the game map.
help.place.use.what: What the voice does with this place. You can tick several.
help.place.use.mark.what: A marker the voice can give to the player.
help.place.use.mark.game: It appears on the map of the player.
help.place.use.mark.tip: Used by "Mark a place on the map" and "Show a neighbourhood". With no reward set, the voice also gives the marker of one of these places after a mission.
help.place.use.target.what: The place aimed at by a mission: a tile inside the building.
help.place.use.target.game: It is circled on the map of the player during the mission.
help.place.use.drop.what: A dead drop: the place where the player leaves things, or where a reward is put.
help.place.use.drop.tip: Delivery and papers missions need at least one.
help.place.use.landing.what: A trade meeting spot, where the merchant meets the players.
help.place.use.landing.tip: Used by the Trade panel of step 5.
help.mission.type.what: The kind of mission the voice gives.
help.mission.type.tip: The game itself checks that the mission is done: the voice decides nothing.
help.mission.story.what: The reason the voice gives for its request.
help.mission.story.game: The AI receives it with the mission and tells it to the player.
help.mission.story.example: I need to know what is left of my clinic.
help.mission.target.game: It is circled on the map of the player.
help.mission.target.tip: The barricade, relay and watch kinds need a place. To scout or clear, with no place, the game picks a building near the player.
help.mission.drops.what: The dead drops where the player may leave the things.
help.mission.drops.game: All of them are circled on the map, and the player leaves them wherever they like.
help.mission.drops.tip: Nothing ticked: all the dead drops of the voice.
help.mission.weight.what: Whether the voice offers this mission rarely, normally or often among several.
help.mission.weight.tip: Normally by default. Often comes up twice as much as Normally.
help.mission.after.what: This mission is only offered once another mission is done.
help.mission.after.game: The player discovers the missions one after the other.
help.mission.scope.what: For "Only after": who must have completed the first mission.
help.mission.scope.character.what: The player themselves must have completed the first mission.
help.mission.scope.team.what: The whole team of the player counts (their faction, or just them if they have none).
help.mission.sets_state.what: A word the voice remembers once the mission is done: the state of the story.
help.mission.sets_state.game: The AI is reminded of it on every call. Other mods can read it.
help.mission.sets_state.tip: A word made of a-z, 0-9 and _. Say in its personality what this state changes for it.
help.mission_type.scout.game: The player visits a building, then reports what they saw.
help.mission_type.clear.game: The player kills the zombies around a place.
help.mission_type.signal.game: The player lights a Signal Smoke signal at the requested place.
help.mission_type.barricade.game: The player boards up outside windows and doors with planks or metal sheets.
help.mission_type.barricade.tip: A place is needed. Only barricades built during the mission count.
help.mission_type.deliver.game: The player leaves the requested items at a dead drop. Drops at several places add up.
help.mission_type.deliver.tip: At least one dead drop is needed.
help.mission_type.retrieve.game: The player finds the ID card of a missing person and leaves it at a dead drop.
help.mission_type.retrieve.tip: At least one dead drop is needed.
help.mission_type.item.game: The game puts a precious item at the chosen place. The player finds it and leaves it at a dead drop.
help.mission_type.item.tip: A place and a dead drop are needed.
help.mission_type.relay.game: The player puts a powered, switched-on radio that can transmit high up (an upper floor or the roof).
help.mission_type.relay.tip: A place is needed. Switched off, without power or removed, the radio no longer counts.
help.mission_type.route.game: The player goes through several places in order, on foot or by vehicle, then reports.
help.mission_type.route.tip: Only the next stop is circled on the map.
help.mission_type.watch.game: The player stays near a place for a few game hours, then tells what they saw.
help.mission_type.watch.tip: A place is needed. Time counts in game hours: it stops when the game is paused.
help.mission_type.barricade.count.what: How many outside windows and doors to barricade.
help.param.collect_hours.what: The game hours before the voice picks up the things at the dead drop.
help.param.collect_hours.game: The pick-up happens out of the sight of the player.
help.param.items.what: The category of the requested items. Only items of this category count.
help.param.items.tip: With no category, the voice asks for 6 bandages or torn sheets.
help.param.quantity.what: How many items are asked: one number, or two numbers for a range.
help.param.quantity.game: The game draws the number at the start of the mission, then it no longer changes.
help.param.item.what: The full name of the item to find: Module.Type.
help.param.label.what: How the voice calls the item.
help.param.label.game: The player hears it in the request.
help.param.points.what: The places to go through, in order: from 2 to 8 places set as "mission place".
help.param.points.game: The player passes a point by going within 8 tiles of its centre.
help.param.points.tip: Never the same place twice in a row.
help.param.hours.what: The number of game hours to stay at the watch post.
help.param.hours.game: The player must stay within 6 tiles of the place.
help.param_kind.category.what: A category of items, chosen from the list.
help.param_kind.item.what: An item of the game: type its name and pick it in the list.
help.param_kind.place.what: One of the places of the voice, chosen from the list.
help.param_kind.places.what: Several places of the voice, in order.
help.param_kind.range.what: One number, or two numbers for a range: the game draws one.
help.param_kind.skill.what: A game skill, chosen from the list.
help.rewards.pool.what: The list of possible rewards after a successful mission.
help.rewards.pool.game: After each successful mission, the game draws just one at random, following their chances. The player also gains reputation.
help.rewards.pool.example: Bag of supplies: Often; a frequency: Rarely
help.rewards.pool.tip: A reward that is impossible at that moment is not drawn. With no list, the voice gives the marker of one of its places.
help.ui.reward_weight.what: Whether this reward comes out rarely, normally or often against the others. Often comes out twice as much as Normally, which comes out twice as much as Rarely. Next to its name, the page says roughly how often it comes out.
help.ui.reward_weight.example: A medical bag on Often and a lesson on Normally: the bag comes out about 2 times in 3.
help.reward.cache.what: A bag of items of one category.
help.reward.cache.game: The bag is put at the first dead drop of the voice. The items are real, in randomly drawn amounts.
help.reward.cache.tip: At least one place is needed. The player gets the marker of the dead drop, seen only by them.
help.reward.frequency.game: It is written in the notebook of the player.
help.reward.frequency.tip: The possible voices are set with "shares" (step 3).
help.reward.stashmap.what: A map that leads to a hidden stash of the game, not yet searched.
help.reward.stashmap.tip: Only one per player and per voice.
help.reward.lesson.game: The game gives 25 experience points as a base, with a cap of 100 per day.
help.reward.lesson.tip: A character with no bonus in this skill only gets a quarter of it.
help.shared_category.ammo.what: Ammunition: 9 mm bullets and shotgun shells.
help.shared_category.food.what: Tinned food: beans, soup and corn.
help.shared_category.medical.what: Medical supplies: bandages, disinfectant and pills.
help.shared_category.radio.what: Radio gear: a walkie-talkie and batteries.
help.shared_category.tools.what: Tools: a hammer, a screwdriver and nails.
help.ui.own_categories.what: Your own lists of items, for deliveries and bags of supplies.
help.ui.own_categories.game: A category fills a bag, or sets what the player is asked to deliver.
help.ui.item_browser.what: Opens the list of every item of the game: search by name, filter by category, click an item to pick it.
help.ui.item_browser.game: Each line gives the item's name as the player sees it, its category in the game's inventory, its type (Module.Type, what the sheet keeps) and its weight.
help.ui.item_browser.example: Category "Food", search "whiskey": Bottle of Whiskey, Base.Whiskey, 1.7 kg.
help.ui.item_browser.tip: In a list of items, each click (or Enter) adds a line and the window stays open: add several items at once, then "Done". Escape closes the window.
help.ui.item_category.what: Shows only the items of one category, the one the game shows in the inventory.
help.ui.item_category.tip: With a category and no search, the whole category is listed in alphabetical order.
help.category.item.what: An item of the list, with its amount: Module.Type:amount.
help.category.item.game: The game draws an amount within the range.
help.ui.description.what: A few words to remind you who this voice is.
help.ui.description.tip: For you only: the game does not read it.
help.ui.prompt.what: The only description of the character: past, skills, what it hides, tone and radio rules. The AI reads this text to play the voice.
help.ui.prompt.example: You are Mae Tolliver, 67, a retired schoolteacher...
help.ui.prompt.game: What the voice learns about the world (deaths, places, missions, news) comes from the game while it is played.
help.ui.prompt.tip: Write it in English, in the second person. Tell it to stay in character and to answer in short sentences. No server secrets: the AI can repeat anything. Never write how a place is now (who holds it, what is surrounded): it would become false. A secret goes here too, with the rule that the voice never tells it.
help.trade.section.what: Trade: the voice sells its stock on the radio and delivers in secret, never showing itself.
help.trade.section.game: No trader ever appears in game. The player's first firm offer on the radio books a passage for their group: the trader gives the place, the night and the signal, and the place is marked on the map. The player puts a bag with the payment within 3 squares of the place, then goes out of sight; back there, the bag holds the goods.
help.trade.section.example: 2 boxes of shells for a bottle of whiskey: at 2 am, lamp lit at the dock, the player hears the boat land, drops the bag and walks away; an hour later the whiskey is in the bag.
help.trade.section.tip: A bag that does not cover the price is cheating: nothing is taken. A passage can be called off (patrol, checkpoint, sweep, helicopter, storm), and the trader leaves if there is never a quiet moment.
help.trade.landing.what: The meeting place with the merchant.
help.trade.landing.game: The place is marked on the map of the group that booked, and only theirs. The player puts a bag with the payment there, within 3 squares of the place.
help.trade.landing.tip: Only the places ticked "trade meeting" in step 4 are offered.
help.trade.arrival.game: Boat or road: during the window, the player shows the signal on the spot, then hears the trader arrive. Dead drop: no signal, the payment waits in the container of the place.
help.trade.arrival.boat.what: A boat lands at the meeting place.
help.trade.arrival.boat.game: During the window, the player shows a lit lamp in hand or a red flare (Signal Smoke) on the spot; they hear the boat's engine as it lands.
help.trade.arrival.road.what: A van parks by the road.
help.trade.arrival.road.game: Same signals as for the boat; you hear the door of the van parked by the roadside.
help.trade.arrival.cache.game: No signal: the player leaves the payment in the container of the place (bin, mailbox) before the hour, and the goods are put there out of sight.
help.trade.arrival.cache.tip: Like the traders of Rosewood, Ekron or Fallas Lake. No noise.
help.trade.every_days.what: One visit of the merchant every N game days.
help.trade.every_days.game: The trader only comes back after this many days; each passage is booked by a firm offer on the radio.
help.trade.hours.what: The time window of the meeting, in game time.
help.trade.hours.game: On the booked night, the player must be at the meeting during this window to show the signal (not for a dead drop).
help.trade.hours.tip: The end may be after midnight: from 23:00 to 01:00.
help.trade.delay_hours.what: The game hours during which nobody must see the place before the exchange.
help.trade.delay_hours.game: The trader only comes if nobody has been within 100 squares (in x and in y) for that time. Coming back too early resets the wait; gone long enough, the exchange is done when you come back.
help.trade.delay_hours.tip: About 1 game hour by default. Optional.
help.trade.margin.what: The share the merchant keeps on each exchange: the lowest and the highest, in percent.
help.trade.item.what: A good the trader brings: the item, then the quantity (from… to…). Add one line per item.
help.trade.item.game: The amount is drawn on each visit. A trader only sells items that have a price in the trade, so the item list of the stock only offers those.
help.trade.item.tip: Type the item's name ("battery", "bandage") and pick it in the list. Its weight is shown for information: the game reads it by itself. If the trade has lots, the amount can come from a lot.
help.trade.group.what: A lot of goods that share a total: its name, how many items in all (from… to…) and, if you want, at most how many different kinds.
help.trade.group.game: On each visit the game draws the total, then shares it among the items of the lot.
help.trade.group.example: seeds, from 3 to 8 in all, at most 4 kinds
help.trade.group.tip: In "Goods", pick "In the lot" for each item of the lot. The game refuses a lot without items.
help.note.item.what: The item that carries the note, written Module.Type.
help.note.item.tip: Use the item the mod provides for notes. A new voice writes its text (text) instead.
help.note.key.what: The base name of the texts of the note.
help.note.key.game: The player reads these texts by inspecting the note.
help.note.key.tip: The texts must exist in the translations of the mod. A new voice writes its text (text) instead.
help.note.loot.what: Where the note can be found in the loot: the name of a list of the game, and whether it is rare, normal or frequent there. Add one line per list.
help.note.loot.game: The player finds it while searching, then reads the frequency.
help.note.loot.tip: Often makes it twice as easy to find as Normally.
help.note.glovebox.what: Where the note can be found in the glove boxes of vehicles: the list, and Rarely, Normally or Often.
help.note.corpse.what: A dead body carrying a walkie-talkie may have the note on it.
help.note.text.what: The text of the note, one line per entry; %1 is replaced by the frequency of the voice. The note is the handwritten note of the mod.
help.note.text.game: The player finds the note in the loot and reads this text by inspecting it.
help.note.text.tip: 8 lines of 40 bytes at most, without < > ^; one line must hold %1.
